resolved.was: The configurator could not be operated by keyboard at all: all six switches were <span class="toggle">, every field label was a <span class="fld-l">, and condition rows after the first emitted an empty label.
resolved.fix: Every switch is now <input type="checkbox" class="switch" role="switch"> inside its own <label>, named by aria-labelledby on the row title. Every field label is a real <label for>, emitted on every condition row and .sr-only after the first. The pointer cursor now only sits on things that are operable.
verified_by: Space on #c-engine turns the rule on
all selects report labels.length > 0
AUTO-3 and AUTO-4 gates pass
0 .toggle elements remain

resolved.was: "Nothing is pre-filled" was false: the first turn-on revealed an authored condition row (Invoice note is equal to Memo on statement) and Save was immediately enabled, committing a rule narrower than the default matcher it replaced.
resolved.fix: cfg.conditions starts empty (the R16 empty-box state), so the first turn-on presents scope defaults only. The reference card now says the saved setup does not change until Save, and names what the suggested starting rule contains as a starting point to review.
verified_by: first turn-on has 0 condition rows
the empty box is explained as scope-only

resolved.was: The query panel printed DocNumber = 'INV-1042' for every source, from a ternary whose two branches were the same string, and printed the DocNumber line even when the source resolved to absent.
resolved.fix: sqlBlock() derives the literal from the same resolve() call the engine uses, states the resolved value for the selected source in the preamble, and when the source resolves to absent it drops the DocNumber line and says so.
verified_by: 4 sources produce 4 different literals
a blank metadata key drops the clause and shows the note

resolved.was: With "Apply payments to invoices" off, the overlay declared itself inert and then reported "Applied — Applied to INV-1042", kept the query titled "will send", showed a green Custom rule chip on GSP, and the warning contained no action.
resolved.fix: The prerequisite-off state is inert everywhere: the simulator prints "Nothing runs", plain terms is prefixed "Once it is on, Synder would…" and switches to would-phrasing, the query panel is titled "would send", the footer says saved-but-inert, and both chips read "Custom rule (inactive)" in grey. The warning banner now carries the prerequisite switch itself.
verified_by: simulator shows Nothing runs and never Applied
GSP chip reads Custom rule (inactive)
the in-banner switch flips the prerequisite

resolved.was: "is empty" greyed out the On the invoice select — the only field it tests — while leaving On the payment editable, still resolved the unread payment source and skipped the row as not applicable when absent, and still demanded a metadata key nothing read.
resolved.fix: For value-less operands the gating is inverted: On the payment is disabled and muted, On the invoice stays editable. The engine skips resolve() for those rows so they always apply, validation no longer demands a key, and the row states "the invoice's <target> is empty. Nothing on the payment is used".
verified_by: #cs-0 disabled, #ct-0 enabled
Save unblocked with a blank key
the run log says the row always applies

resolved.was: The shared cancel-sync value committed instantly on GSP but was a discardable draft in the overlay, and while any blocking error was present it had no commit path at all. Validation also ran with the rule switched off, so a retained error kept Save disabled with no error field on screen — the integration could not be returned to the default matcher.
resolved.fix: The overlay copy commits on flip like the GSP row, writing to both cfg and saved and repainting GSP, independent of the Save gate. validate() returns early when the rule is off, so a retained-but-off configuration is always saveable.
verified_by: flipping it in the overlay lands on GSP without Save
it survives a discard
an off rule carrying a blank-key error saves and returns GSP to Synder default

resolved.was: Three labels called the candidate set "open invoices" while the query deliberately had no balance filter; "processed as usual" was never translated into a document, leaving it unstated whether income is counted twice; and the inheritance helper framed a missing customer as data completeness rather than mis-attribution.
resolved.fix: Prototype-authored copy says "matching invoice", and section 1, the query panel and plain terms all state that unpaid, partly paid and fully paid invoices are candidates because balance is not filtered. The no-match outcome names the document — Sales Receipt, so no existing invoice is settled — in the outcome row, the simulator verdict and plain terms, flagged as ASSUMPTION A5 because the FDD does not name it. The inheritance helper now states the attribution consequence, and warns when Customer is off while the invoice number is compared more loosely than "is equal to". The two verbatim production setting names are left untouched.
verified_by: example C names the Sales Receipt
the loose-comparison warning fires
the candidate-set sentence renders in section 1 and the query panel

resolved.was: The admin-gated date switch rendered at full opacity, pixel-identical to the live switches above and below it, and clicking it did nothing at all — KF-4, the product's densest dead-click pattern.
resolved.fix: It is now a disabled switch inside .tog.dis, the same dimmed treatment the plan-gated master switch already uses, keeping the lock glyph and adding an actionable next step (Ask Synder to enable it). Because the kit paints every disabled switch in the grey off-track, a locked on switch keeps the on track colour and also spells its state out as a word, so "on" never rests on a dimmed colour alone.
verified_by: #c-date isDisabled
wrapper opacity < 1
the hint names who can lift it
screenshot at 3x confirms the on state reads as on

resolved.was: Cancel, close and Escape discarded the whole rule with no prompt and no undo; Escape was bound on document with no dirty check and no target check, so it fired while a select was open or a field was being edited; and the overlay was a plain div with no role, no accessible name, no focus move on open and no focus return on close.
resolved.fix: A dirty check compares the working copy with the saved rule and routes close, Cancel and Escape through a Discard your changes? alertdialog. Escape belongs to the field or dropdown first (INPUT/SELECT/TEXTAREA are ignored), then to the prompt, then to the dialog. The overlay is role=dialog aria-modal=true aria-labelledby, focus moves to Close on open, Tab is contained, and focus returns to the trigger on every close path.
verified_by: Escape mid-typing neither closes nor prompts
Escape dismisses the prompt only
Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the dialog
focus returns to #g-open

resolved.was: Every blocking error was a bare div.err with no id, no role, no aria-live, not referenced by aria-describedby and with no aria-invalid on the field. The footer reported only a count, the failing row could be far off screen with no jump affordance, and the disabled Save left the tab order entirely.
resolved.fix: paintErrors() gives each error an id and role=alert, points the field's aria-describedby at it and sets aria-invalid, and rewrites a slot only when its content changes so keystrokes do not re-announce. The footer is a live region that names the first blocking error and offers a Show me button that scrolls the row into view and focuses the field. Save is aria-disabled rather than disabled, so it keeps its place in the tab order, and clicking it jumps to the first error instead of doing nothing.
verified_by: #err-inherit has role=alert
the field points at it with aria-invalid
the footer names the error and offers the jump
Save is focusable and clickable while blocked

resolved.was: A blocking free-text "Metadata key" field with the placeholder "e.g. invoices" and nothing on screen saying what a key is or where to find the one this store uses.
resolved.fix: Labelled "Which Stripe field holds it?" on the scope row and "Which Stripe field?" on condition rows, with a line saying where to look (Stripe → any payment → Metadata, the name on the left of the pair), a link to Stripe's metadata documentation, and a datalist of the known keys. The blocking message is now "Name the Stripe field that holds the reference."
verified_by: the label, the where-to-find line and the datalist all render
the error text no longer contains "metadata key"

resolved.was: 10 text nodes below WCAG AA contrast, including grey_50 body text at 4.26:1 and the two status chips at 3.54:1 and 3.81:1.
resolved.fix: A commented local token extension derives --color-grey-60 and --color-green-dark from existing tokens with color-mix (no raw hex), overrides --text-secondary and --text-placeholder, and darkens the grey and green chip inks. The decorative | separator became a real 1px divider with no text node.
verified_by: 147 text nodes measured, worst 4.70:1, gate passes
resolved.note: grey_50 failing AA on white for text under 18.66px is a design-system issue, not a prototype one — the kit needs a darker step.

resolved.was: The plan gate stated the requirement but offered no action, so the row was a dead end for a Starter user.
resolved.fix: A Compare plans link sits beside the disabled Configure button on the gated row, and inside the overlay's Starter error block.

resolved.was: An out-of-range day count was silently rewritten to the maximum, with the limit stated nowhere in the UI.
resolved.fix: The field label states the accepted range (1–365) and a clamp shows an inline note naming the limit that was applied.

resolved.was: Switching cancel-sync on was described as "nothing is created" with no word on where the payment then goes.
resolved.fix: Both surfaces now say the payment stays in Synder with a Canceled status, can be synced again once a matching invoice exists, and nothing is deleted from the books.

resolved.was: Both hints described the DocNumber field as holding 21 characters, where the spec defines at most 21.
resolved.fix: Both now read "at most 21 characters", keeping the truncation sentence. Asserted in the verification run.

resolved.was: 16 padding values off the 4/8px grid (14px and 10px paddings).
resolved.fix: Snapped to the grid across panels, rows, banners, cards and the table. The gate now covers more selectors than the round-1 check did.

resolved.was: A single ArrowUp fired change, re-rendered the overlay body, replaced the input node and dropped focus to <body>; two further presses left the value stuck at 91.
resolved.fix: The day count never re-renders. oninput and onchange both do a targeted refresh of the derived text (row title, window, plain terms, query, simulator, footer) and leave the input node in place.
verified_by: two ArrowUps reach 92 with focus still on the field

resolved.was: Escape while typing in the metadata key — the standard gesture for reverting a field — closed the overlay and discarded everything.
resolved.fix: Covered by theme 9's Escape target check.

resolved.was: All four cards were divs with no role, no tabindex and no aria-checked, and Tab went straight past them, so by keyboard only the pre-selected outcome could ever be evaluated.
resolved.fix: A role=radiogroup of role=radio buttons with roving tabindex and arrow-key navigation; focus follows the selection.
verified_by: ArrowDown moves the selection and focus follows it

resolved.found_while_fixing: disclosure panels collapsed on a same-frame re-render
resolved.was: The open state of In plain terms / the query / the simulator was captured from the toggle event, which Chromium delivers a frame late — so changing a control immediately after opening a panel collapsed it again.
resolved.fix: renderOverlay() calls snapshotDisc() and reads the live .open state instead of waiting for the event.

resolved.found_while_fixing: a blocked Save was a dead click for a mouse user
resolved.was: The kit's .btn-disabled sets pointer-events:none, so with Save aria-disabled the click-to-jump-to-error never fired from a mouse.
resolved.fix: .btn[aria-disabled="true"] restores pointer-events with a not-allowed cursor. Asserted in the verification run.
